question: Your rover ends its square away from the start. Why does overwriting only its last pose not fix the drifted map?
options: The last pose is locked once it has been measured
Every earlier pose along the path stays bent
A loop closure gives no usable measurement
explanation: The drift built up along the whole path, so every earlier pose is bent too and fixing only the last one leaves them wrong.

question: You build your rover's pose graph. What is an odometry edge in it?
options: A spring joining every pose to the start
A spring between two neighbouring poses
A landmark that two poses both stand next to
explanation: An odometry edge holds one measured move. It says where pose j should be seen from pose i, like a spring between them.

question: You solve your rover's pose graph. Why hold pose 0 fixed?
options: To save memory, since pose 0 never needs to be updated
Moving or turning the whole map changes no residual
Pose 0 is the only pose the scanner measured directly
explanation: Moving or turning the whole map does not change any residual, so without an anchor three directions (x, y and heading) stay undetermined.

question: You solve your rover's pose graph with Gauss-Newton. What happens to the cost between iterations here?
explanation: Each Gauss-Newton step is chosen to cut the cost, and in this well-posed graph the real cost does not go up from one iteration to the next.

question: Your rover thinks it recognises the start, but the match is false. What does a wrong loop closure do?
options: Bends the map worse than having no closure
Nothing, since the solver ignores bad edges
Improves the map even if the match is false
explanation: The solver trusts every edge, so a false one pulls the poses wrong.

question: Your rover closes the loop and several earlier poses move. Why does the correction reach those poses?
options: Every free pose is a variable solved together
The map is rebuilt from scratch each time
Old poses are overwritten by the last pose
explanation: The solver treats every pose except pose 0 as a variable and changes them all at once, so the closing spring pulls the whole path.
